ambiguities_or_notes: The opening Tolstoy thesis, four numbered readings, all attributions, and the closing warning are represented.
The page 39→40 boundary is preserved before item 2.
The Channing passage retains the repeated “man/person,” “soul,” and developmental language rather than compressing it.
The Emerson passage preserves the chapel/temple image and the contrast between reading in a book and in one’s soul.
The Kant-derived distinction between intellectual and moral knowledge is preserved without importing Kantian terminology absent from Tolstoy’s Russian.
Thoreau’s unusual “above morality” formulation is kept literally.
